Concepts – Abstract mental units that make it possible to organize phenomena under general classes and to make them comprehensible in language.
Categories – The a priori forms of thought of the mind (such as causality and substance) that function as the operating system of cognition and determine how we can think about objects.
Synthesis – The central cognitive operation through which the brain combines different perceptual data into a unified picture of reality.
Understanding – The active cognitive faculty that brings the diversity of perception under concepts and makes objective experience possible through rules (categories).
Forms of View – The a priori structures of space and time that function as necessary formats to bring disordered sensory data into an experiential order.
Productive imagination – The mediating authority that links the visual material with the intellectual concepts and generates the mental images of our world simulation.
Sensations – The as yet unstructured material of perception, which must first be formed into a recognizable object through synthesis and categories.
Appearances - The results of perception as they are given to us within the boundaries of space, time and categories of understanding (phenomena), as opposed to the unknowable 'thing in itself'.
Regulatory Ideas - Guiding principles of reason that, although not provable objects, serve as necessary landmarks to complete research and the world model.
Sensuality – The passive cognitive faculty through which we are affected. It provides the raw material of sensations, which is only structured through the forms of perception of space and time.
Judgments – Logical combinations of concepts that make statements about the nature of the world and form the basis of our knowledge.
Reason – The highest cognitive faculty that strives for the unity of knowledge and goes beyond reason to develop regulatory ideas for a closed worldview.
The interface where the 'Superintelligence' project connects human intuition with AI computational logic.
Inversion principle - A dialectical law of world simulation in which an extreme overcontrol of the expectation vectors provokes a system collapse that manifests the opposite event.

Human brain - The biological hardware interface that uses highly energy-efficient processes (approx. 20W) to generate a stable, four-dimensional world model from the highly complex wave functions of external reality.

This is a simple, ever-improving design of a reality model with a human brain at the center. First of all, a human brain is at the center. But this could gradually replace an AI model with its own program or computer core. The extensive presentation of “expectation” is intended to describe the influence of human “thinking” on reality. This is intended to explain how the future could shape itself without using chance.

Observer (in quantum mechanics) – In the Copenhagen interpretation, the actor who determines a concrete result through measurement. Physically, every interaction is a measurement, not necessarily consciousness. It is unclear whether the human brain plays a special role in this or is just another decoherence channel.

Decoherence – Process in which interference terms become unmeasurable due to uncontrolled entanglement with the environment. Explains why the brain does not perceive superpositions and instead receives a stable 3D model of the world. Mechanism mathematically established, complete explanation of the measurement problem but incomplete.

Mathematics of quantum mechanics - formalism based on Hilbert space, complex wave functions, Hermitian operators and the Schroedinger equation. It is the exact calculation rule with which the brain translates the data source into predictions. High precision, no internal contradictions.

entities.id: Measurement problem / collapse of the wave function
entities.description: Measurement problem / collapse of the wave function – question of why a measurement only gives a single result even though the Schroedinger equation is continuous and deterministic. Is the collapse physically real or just an update of information in the human logic model? Core of the conflict between the outside world and the 3D world model.

Predictive Brain Theory – theory that the brain is not a passive camera, but an active inference machine: top-down predictions are compared with bottom-up sensor data, prediction errors are minimized. Formally about Bayesian inference. Explains how the 3D world model is rendered as a controlled hallucination.

Quantum effects in biology - evidence of quantum coherence in photosynthesis (energy transport), entanglement in the bird compass (cryptochrome), tunneling in enzymes and the sense of smell. Shows that the human brain is not completely decoherent and evolution could use quantum effects.

Quantum Mechanics – The Fundamental Theory of the Microworld. It describes the outside world not as a set of classical objects, but as a spectrum of probability amplitudes. The brain then renders a stable, classic macro world (3D world model) in the human logic model.

Quantum Brain – family of hypotheses (including Penrose-Hameroff Orch-OR) that consciousness is based on non-trivial quantum computations in microtubules and collapse occurs through objective reduction (gravity-induced). Would mean that the brain is not a classical computer, but rather uses quantum processes directly.

Quantum Predictive Brain (QPB) – 2022 proposal in Frontiers in Psychology: Replaces classical Bayesian probability in predictive brain theory with quantum probability. This allows cognitive phenomena such as order effects and contextuality to be modeled. The brain therefore uses quantum-like logic without necessarily being a quantum computer.

Superposition – principle that a quantum system can exist in several classical states at the same time (e.g. spin up + down). Confirmed experimentally in double slits, interferometry and quantum computers. The human logic model cannot render superposition directly and forces it into a classic either/or representation.

Unruh effect - prediction of quantum field theory: An accelerated observer perceives the vacuum as a thermal bath with temperature T = a*hbar/(2*pi*c*kB). Shows that particle number and vacuum depend on the observer state. Direct experimental confirmation is lacking, but mathematically robustly derived from established QFT.

Entanglement – Non-classical correlation between two particles described as a common system, regardless of distance. Bell inequalities violated experimentally (Nobel Prize 2022). Challenges the local 3D world model and shows that the brain renders locality as a UI simplification.

Wave function – mathematical description of the complete quantum state. |ψ> contains all possible measurement outputs as a superposition. In the context of the main graph: the raw data structure of the outside world, from which the brain extracts a unique 3D world model via decoherence.

Wigner's friend - extension of the measurement problem according to Eugene Wigner: A friend in the laboratory measures a quantum system, while Wigner himself describes the entire laboratory as a superposition. Shows the conflict between two descriptions of reality. Serves as a metaphor for the fact that the 3D world model could be rendered independent of the observer.

entities.id: 1D random walk with drift model for single neuron
entities.description: 1D random walk with drift model for single neuron - Models the membrane potential q as a Markov process between resting potential and firing threshold. Each incoming excitatory input (EPSP) moves the variable one step forward to the threshold, each inhibitory input (IPSP) one step backwards. If the EPSP/IPSP rate is unequal, there is a net drift speed b_f (forward) and b_b (backward). As a Wiener process with SDE dq = b_t dt + sigma dW_t, it explains membrane potential fluctuations, irregular spike trains, trial-to-trial variability and firing irregularity. Basis for Gerstein-Mandelbrot 1964.

entities.id: Nelson's stochastic mechanics - equivalence of Brownian motion and Schroedinger equation
entities.description: Nelson's Stochastic Mechanics - Mathematically exact mapping (Nelson 1966, Guerra & Morato 1983) between Brownian diffusion processes and wave mechanics. Defines forward and backward SDEs dq = b_t dt + sigma dW_t and dq = b*_t dt + sigma dW*_t for EPSP and IPSP driven processes, respectively. Current velocity v = ½(b_t+b*_t) = 1/m_q ∂S/∂q and osmotic velocity u = ½(b_t-b*_t) = sigma/2 ∂_q ln rho. This means exactly i hbar ∂_t psi(q,t) = (-hbar²/2m ∂_q² + V(q)) psi(q,t) with psi = sqrt(rho) exp(iS/hbar) and hbar = m sigma. Every Brownian process has hidden quantum-like coherence structure.

Neural constant hbar = m sigma – analogue to the reduced Planck quantum of action for neuronal media. m is neuronal inductance / inertia of the electrical potential (tendency to hold potential), sigma² = 2D = Var(q)/Δt is diffusion coefficient from variance of membrane potential. hbar can be neuron type dependent or universal. If sigma m = 0, the system is classic. Large hbar would mean that quantum-like effects at the neuron level are not negligible. Can be determined empirically from real data.

entities.id: Osmotic velocity and stochastic potential V_Q
entities.type: Theoretical concept: quantum drift / Bohm potential analogue
entities.description: Osmotic velocity and stochastic potential V_Q – u(q,t) = sigma/2 ∂_q ln rho = hbar/m ∂_q R describes the diffusion pressure. V_Q = -hbar²/2m[(∂_q R)²+∂²_q R] = hbar²/4m[∂²_q rho/rho - (∂_q rho)²/2rho²] is analogous to the Bohm quantum potential. In Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation ∂_t S + 1/2m(∂_q S)² + V + V_Q =0 plus continuity equation ∂_t rho + ∂_q[rho 1/m ∂_q S]=0, V_Q couples amplitude sqrt(rho) and phase S and creates interference/coherence. If V_Q disappears if rho is independent of q or hbar=0, then R and S decouple and the system becomes classic. That's why u is also called 'quantum drift'.

FitzHugh-Nagumo model - Two coupled differential equations for membrane potential q and recovery variable w: dq/dt = q - q³/3 - w + I, dw/dt = epsilon(q+a-bw). Nonlinear term q - q³/3 describes fast activation/deactivation after spike. epsilon controls slow recovery timescale, a,b determine threshold activation, spike duration and recovery. Simplification of the 4D Hodgkin-Huxley model, combining gating variables into a recovery variable w. Established model for neuronal dynamics, cell division, population dynamics.

entities.id: Stochastic FitzHugh-Nagumo model with quantum correction
entities.description: Stochastic FitzHugh-Nagumo model with quantum correction - extension of the FN equations to include additive Wiener processes xi_q(t), xi_w(t) for channel noise through randomly superposed EPSPs/IPSPs: dq/dt = q - q³/3 - w + I + xi_q(t), dw/dt = epsilon(q+a-bw) + xi_w(t). q thus becomes a random variable with drift. Using second order q̈, Lagrange function L = ½ qdot² + ½(b-1)q² - epsilon b/12 q⁴ - epsilon b/2 w², Rayleigh dissipation function R_d and generalized force Q = -(a epsilon + b epsilon + I) becomes Hamiltonian H = ½p² -½(b-1)q² + epsilon b/12 q⁴ + epsilon b/2 w² = ½p²+V(q,w) constructed. Canonical quantization p→ -i hbar ∂_q yields operator Ĥ and Schroedinger equation i hbar ∂_t psi(q,t)=Ĥ psi = (-hbar²/2 ∂²_q + V) psi. This makes stochastic FN dynamics mathematically equivalent to quantum-like wave dynamics, with V_Q as a correction to deterministic spiking rates.

entities.id: Quantum-like coherence through noise – Order from Disorder
entities.description: Quantum-like coherence through noise - Central thesis of the article: Exactly the thermal noise (Brownian motion, channel noise, background activity), which, according to the standard argument, destroys quantum superpositions in the brain through decoherence, creates quantum-like coherence, stability and structure in the electromagnetic region of the neuron. Stochastic fluctuations have hidden phase-amplitude correlation via psi = sqrt(rho) exp(iS/hbar). Example of 'order from disorder'. Reverses the reasoning: Noise is not only a disruptive factor, but also a source of non-classical behavior.

entities.id: Subthreshold oscillations as coherent states of the harmonic oscillator
entities.description: Subthreshold oscillations as coherent states - For small oscillations around rest potential, FN potential becomes a harmonic oscillator: Energy U = ½(CV²+LI²) or H = p²/2m + ½ m omega² q² with m = L (inductance), q = C V, p = L I, omega = 1/sqrt(LC). Schroedinger equation provides stationary levels E_n = hbar omega(n+½) with zero point energy hbar omega/2 and coherent states |alpha⟩ = D(alpha)|0⟩ with D(alpha)=exp(alpha a†-alpha* a). Prediction: ⟨q⟩ = sqrt(2hbar/momega) |alpha| cos(omega t - phi) with scattering (sigma_q)² = hbar/2m omega. Measurable with high-resolution patch clamp techniques.

entities.id: Empirical determination of hbar via variance and inductance
entities.description: Empirical determination of hbar via variance and inductance: (a) diffusion coefficient sigma² = 2D = Var(q)/Δt from variance of q = C V at subthreshold fluctuations, (b) inductance m = L from adapting voltage oscillations to LCR circuit or from equivalent inductance through piezoelectric effect of the cell membrane. Myelin, as a lipid-rich substance around axons, provides large effective inductance, although pure unmyelinated membrane has small inductance. Early measurement on squid giant axon showed small L, mammal myelin could explain large L. hbar = m sigma. Whether hbar varies or is universal remains an open question.

Quantum phenomena (superposition, blurring) function as a 'lazy evaluation': the world is only "rendered" into a definitive state in the microcosm when an interaction (measurement) takes place. This saves enormous computing resources in the simulation of space-time.

entities.id: Dark matter in the cosmic microwave background radiation
entities.description: The dependence of the observed anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background radiation on the matter composition of the early universe. The measured structure of the cosmic microwave background is consistent with a significant non-baryonic matter component in the lambda-CDM model and represents important evidence for the dark matter model, independent of galaxy dynamics.

The cosmological model of a dark matter component whose particles were non-relativistic at the epoch relevant to the formation of cosmic structures. Cold Dark Matter forms a central component of the Lambda CDM standard model and successfully describes the development of large-scale structures. The term describes the dynamic properties of the postulated matter and does not yet identify its microscopic nature.

A socially shared reference point—typically a past success, a widely accepted narrative, or an institutional precedent—that anchors a group's prevailing expectation against recalibration. Collective expectation anchors operationalize the cementing mechanism at the group level: they act as an external validation that reinforces the group simulation and increases the threshold at which new sensory or evidentiary data triggers a reversal search. They differ from individual expectation anchors in that their authority is based on a social consensus and not on a personal story.

A sequential process of diffusion in which a prevailing expectation spreads across institutional layers - from leadership to middle management to the operational level, or from an institutional body to dependent bodies - and is reinforced at each stage by authority and formal confirmation. Each institutional level that adopts the prevailing expectation increases legitimacy, effectively increasing the calibration weight of the expectation and reducing the likelihood that lower levels will initiate a reverse diagnosis. Cascades differ from simple social diffusion in that they use institutional authority and resource allocation as reinforcement mechanisms, rather than just social conformity.

A social or institutional mechanism that systematically increases the strength and persistence of a dominant group expectation, thereby raising the threshold required to trigger a collective reversal. Amplifiers of social reversal include narrative reinforcement, institutional support, resource provision, and public explanation—each of which increases the cost of expectation revision and the social penalty for dissent. Unlike individual-level reverse reinforcers such as sunk costs, social reinforcers derive their power from collective coordination and the expectation of a coordinated response.

entities.type: Transition of the collective expectation phase
entities.description: The discontinuous shift in which a group's dominant expectation collapses and is replaced by an expectation-seeking phase, analogous to a physical phase transition in that the shift is threshold dependent, rapid relative to the previous stable phase, and irreversible without significant recalibration. During the transitions of the collective expectation phase, the social reversal reinforcers that previously reinforced the prevailing expectation reverse their polarity and begin to reinforce the search for a new expectation, resulting in a rapid collective reversal. The transition represents the group-level analogue of the individual expectation reversal, but with higher thresholds, longer latencies, and a more abrupt onset.

entities.type: Transition of the collective expectation phase
entities.description: The minimum aggregate prediction error – summed across group members or institutional signals – required to initiate a transition of the collective expectation phase. The collective reversal threshold is higher than the average individual reversal threshold because social conformity pressure mechanisms and social reversal amplifiers filter out individual reversal signals before they aggregate. The threshold is modulated by the strength of the dominant group expectation, the degree of institutional commitment, and the presence or absence of collective security posture practices that maintain calibration.

A condition in which an institution receives sufficient prediction error signals to initiate an expectations revision, but is unable to complete the correction because institutional lock-in dynamics, social reversal reinforcers, and authority-based cascade mechanisms suppress the reversal process. The failure of an institutional correction is the analogue of the individual's calcification of expectations at the group level and results in the prevailing expectation remaining until an external social tipping trigger forces a transition in the collective expectation phase - typically at a much higher cost than previous voluntary corrections would have required. The failure of the correction is a leading indicator of an impending collective trend reversal on a large scale.

A publicly visible indicator that a group or institution is operating within a collective security situation - such as the presence of active channels for dissent, regular external scenario testing, or the explicit recognition of the uncertainty of expectations in official communication. Group-level safety signals calibrate the prevailing group expectation by signaling that the institution is not fully committed to the dominant prediction, thereby reducing the social penalty for individual expectation revision and lowering the collective reversal threshold. The absence of safety signals is a diagnostic indicator of increased risk of institutional corrective failure.

The group-level causal process by which shared prevailing expectations produce a reversal effect that spreads to multiple individuals simultaneously through social synchronization. Unlike individual reversal trajectories, this mechanism is reinforced by mutual reinforcement between actors, making the collective reversal faster, more severe, and more difficult to interrupt once initiated. It explains why reversal effects in social systems are disproportionately destructive compared to individual cases.

The process by which individual expectations within a group converge into a single dominant expectation through social feedback loops, communication cascades, and shared reference points. Through synchronization, the collective dominance ratio increases faster than the expectations of an individual alone could change. Once synchronization is complete, the group is maximally vulnerable to collective reversal because no internal divergent expectation can break the cascade.

The single agent causal path through which a person's internally prevailing expectation produces a reversal effect when real-world outcomes contradict it. The individual path is determined by the cognitive load at the moment of contradiction, the prior investment in the prevailing expectation and the availability of alternative explanatory frameworks. Unlike collective reversals, individual reversals can be interrupted by private reassessment before social propagation reinforces the effect.

The specific event, signal or piece of information whose arrival in a saturated expectation system causes the threshold to be crossed and the reversal sequence to begin. The trigger itself does not have to be large - its effect is disproportionate since the system is already in a warning state before the reversal. Understanding trigger events allows for earlier identification of what constitutes a dangerous disconfirmation signal within a specific range of expectations.

The self-sustaining impulse of a reversal effect after the threshold has been crossed, which maintains and reinforces the reversed expectation orientation even after the original trigger has passed. Inertia is driven by the dynamics of sunk costs, narrative reinterpretations, and societal pressures to conform to the newly prevailing reverse expectation. It explains why reversal effects persist and deepen rather than correcting themselves once triggered, and why early intervention before the threshold is crossed is far more effective than correction after the reversal.

relations.subject: Group dominance patterns
relations.description: The group dominance pattern models how individual dominant expectations synchronize between group members in a shared collective prediction, which functions as an operational dominant expectation at the mesosocial level and extends the dominant expectation mechanism from the individual to the collective level.

relations.subject: institutional_lock_in_the_dynamic
relations.description: Institutional lock-in dynamics applies the cementation principle to institutional contexts in which accumulated resource commitments and reputational capital anchor a dominant expectation against revision in the same structurally irreversible way that cognitive cementation protects individual dominant expectations from correction.

relations.subject: social_conformity pressure mechanism
relations.description: The mechanism of social conformity pressure provides the causal-mechanistic specification of the existing conformity pressure node and explains exactly how individual expectation suppression in favor of group consensus leads to a collective dominant expectation reinforcement in the absence of new external evidence.

relations.subject: Trigger for social tipping point
relations.description: A social tipping trigger is the class of external events and information signals whose significance exceeds the collective reversal threshold, causally activating the tipping point mechanism in collective social systems and initiating the transition from maintaining dominant expectations to seeking expectations.

relations.subject: collective_security posture
relations.description: A collective security posture modulates the formation and persistence of market-dominant expectations by maintaining institutional channels for divergent predictions and regular external calibration, thereby lowering the collective reversal threshold and allowing for earlier voluntary correction before full institutional commitment.

relations.subject: Reversal threshold model
relations.description: The threshold model operationalizes the reversal effect by formalizing the quantitative limit that must be exceeded for the effect to be triggered and transforming the mechanism from a descriptive endpoint to a predictable, monitorable threshold that the security principle can act on before exceeding.

relations.subject: dominance relationship
relations.description: The dominance ratio formalizes the dominant expectation by providing a quantitative measure of its strength relative to all competing expectations in the system, allows for threshold monitoring over time, and replaces the qualitative description of dominance with a trackable parameter.

relations.subject: Expectation saturation index
relations.description: The saturation index operationalizes the prevailing future expectation by measuring the degree to which the system has exhausted its corrective capacity and identifies exactly when this source of danger has reached the level of structural brittleness at which any triggering event becomes catastrophic.

relations.subject: Pre-reversal warning level
relations.description: The pre-reversal warning level combines threshold detection with the activation of the safety principle by identifying the specific time window within which preventive use remains possible. This allows the protection mechanism to function proactively and not just reactively after the reversal has already occurred.

relations.subject: Cascade_of_social_reinforcement
relations.description: The social reinforcement cascade instantiates the mechanism for cementing preconceptions at the collective level and provides the concrete social dynamics through which individual cognitive biases become increasingly anchored in group-level patterns of expectation, which then resist correction until the threshold is crossed.

relations.subject: cognitive_load_at_the_threshold
relations.description: Cognitive load at the threshold moment modulates the reinforcing effect of dominant cognitive biases on the reversal sequence, as high load prevents corrective reappraisal and allows biases to run uncontrolled at the precise moment when accurate processing is most critical.

relations.subject: individual_expectations
relations.description: The individual expectation trajectory refines the static concept of conscious expectations by mapping their development over time from initial formation through reinforcement and anchoring to near-threshold and adds a dynamic process dimension that shows how conscious expectations become increasingly vulnerable to reversals.
